title: How Many Times?: Equal Groups and Early Multiplication
seo_title: Equal Groups and Early Multiplication Class 1 Worksheet with Answers (Joyful Mathematics Chapter 11)
standard_code: Class 1, Joyful Mathematics Chapter 11: How Many Times?
standard_text: Early multiplication: making equal groups, repeated addition, skip counting and arranging objects in rows (summary of NCERT Joyful Mathematics Class 1)
meta_desc: Class 1 How Many Times? worksheet (Joyful Mathematics Chapter 11): equal groups, adding the same number again, skip counting and arrays. 100 picture questions with answers.
key_sub: Skip count to add equal groups quickly.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • Equal groups have the same number in each group.
  • 3 groups of 4 = 4 + 4 + 4 = 12.
  • Skip count: 2, 4, 6, 8 … or 5, 10, 15 ….

Examples

Example

How many legs do 4 birds have?

2 + 2 + 2 + 2

Answer: 8

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Counting the groups instead of the thingsCount everything, or add the group size again and again.
Groups that are not equalEach group must have the same number.

faq.q: Do Class 1 children learn times tables?
faq.a: Not yet: they make equal groups and add the same number again.

items.q: How many counters are there altogether?
items.e: There are 3 groups. Each group has 4. Count: 4, 8, 12. So 3 groups of 4 make 12.

items.q: How many apples are there altogether?
items.e: There are 2 groups. Each group has 5. Count: 5, 10. So 2 groups of 5 make 10.

items.q: How many counters are there altogether?
items.e: There are 4 groups. Each group has 5. Count: 5, 10, 15, 20. So 4 groups of 5 make 20.
There are 5 groups. Each group has 3. Count: 3, 6, 9, 12, 15. So 5 groups of 3 make 15.

items.q: How many counters are there altogether?
items.e: There are 2 groups. Each group has 6. Count: 6, 12. So 2 groups of 6 make 12.

items.q: How many apples are there altogether?
items.e: There are 4 groups. Each group has 2. Count: 2, 4, 6, 8. So 4 groups of 2 make 8.

items.q: What does the picture show?
items.e: Count the rings: 4 groups. Count one ring: 3 in each. So it is 4 groups of 3. 3 groups of 4 mixes up the groups and the number in each group.

items.q: What does the picture show?
items.e: Count the rings: 2 groups. Count one ring: 6 in each. So it is 2 groups of 6. 6 groups of 2 mixes up the groups and the number in each group.

items.q: What does the picture show?
items.e: Count the rings: 5 groups. Count one ring: 4 in each. So it is 5 groups of 4. 4 groups of 5 mixes up the groups and the number in each group.

items.q: What does the picture show?
items.e: Count the rings: 3 groups. Count one ring: 5 in each. So it is 3 groups of 5. 5 groups of 3 mixes up the groups and the number in each group.

items.q: How many groups are there?
items.e: Count the rings: there are 3 groups. 6 is the number in each group.

items.q: How many counters are in each group?
items.e: Look at one ring. It has 2 counters. 5 is the number of groups.

items.q: Is this shared equally?
items.e: The plates have 4 and 3. They are not all the same, so it is not equal. Equal means every plate has the same number.

items.q: Is this shared equally?
items.e: Every plate has 5. They are all the same, so it is equal: 5 on each.
Every plate has 3. They are all the same, so it is equal: 3 on each.

items.q: Is this shared equally?
items.e: The plates have 2, 3 and 2. They are not all the same, so it is not equal. Equal means every plate has the same number.

items.q: Is this shared equally?
items.e: Every plate has 4. They are all the same, so it is equal: 4 on each.

items.q: Make the 2 plates equal. How many grapes must move?
items.e: 8 shared between 2 is 4 each. Move 1 grape from the 5 to the 3. Now both have 4. (Moving 2 makes 3 and 5.)
10 shared between 2 is 5 each. Move 1 strawberry from the 6 to the 4. Now both have 5. (Moving 2 makes 4 and 6.)

items.q: Make the 2 plates equal. How many apples must move?
items.e: 8 shared between 2 is 4 each. Move 2 apples from the 6 to the 2. Now both have 4. (Moving 4 makes 2 and 6.)

items.q: Which addition matches the picture?
items.e: There are 3 groups of 5. Add 5, 3 times: 5 + 5 + 5 = 15.

items.q: Which addition matches the picture?
items.e: There are 4 groups of 2. Add 2, 4 times: 2 + 2 + 2 + 2 = 8.

items.q: Which addition matches the picture?
items.e: There are 2 groups of 7. Add 7, 2 times: 7 + 7 = 14.

items.q: Which addition matches the picture?
items.e: There are 5 groups of 4. Add 4, 5 times: 4 + 4 + 4 + 4 + 4 = 20.
There are 4 groups of 6. Add 6, 4 times: 6 + 6 + 6 + 6 = 24.

items.q: Which is the same as 4 + 4 + 4?
items.e: Count the 4s: there are 3 of them. So it is 3 groups of 4: 3 × 4 = 12. Do not count the + signs.

items.q: Which is the same as 5 + 5?
items.e: Count the 5s: there are 2 of them. So it is 2 groups of 5: 2 × 5 = 10. Do not count the + signs.
Count the 10s: there are 3 of them. So it is 3 groups of 10: 3 × 10 = 30. Do not count the + signs.

items.q: Which is the same as 2 + 2 + 2 + 2 + 2?
items.e: Count the 2s: there are 5 of them. So it is 5 groups of 2: 5 × 2 = 10. Do not count the + signs.

items.q: Which is the same as 6 + 6 + 6 + 6?
items.e: Count the 6s: there are 4 of them. So it is 4 groups of 6: 4 × 6 = 24. Do not count the + signs.

items.q: Which number sentence matches the jumps?
items.e: Count the arrows: 4 jumps of 5. 5, 10, 15, 20. So 4 × 5 = 20.

items.q: Which number sentence matches the jumps?
items.e: Count the arrows: 6 jumps of 2. 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12. So 6 × 2 = 12.

items.q: Which number sentence matches the jumps?
items.e: Count the arrows: 5 jumps of 3. 3, 6, 9, 12, 15. So 5 × 3 = 15.

items.q: Which number sentence matches the jumps?
items.e: Count the arrows: 3 jumps of 10. 10, 20, 30. So 3 × 10 = 30.

items.q: What is 2 × 8?
items.e: 2 × 8 means 2 groups of 8: 8 + 8 = 16.

items.q: What is 4 × 5?
items.e: 4 × 5 means 4 groups of 5: 5 + 5 + 5 + 5 = 20.

items.q: Raju says 3 × 4 = 7. What did he do?
items.e: 3 + 4 = 7. But 3 × 4 means 3 groups of 4: 4 + 4 + 4 = 12. Raju added the two numbers.

items.q: Pooja writes 6 + 6 + 6 + 6 + 6 = 30. Which multiplication is the same?
items.e: There are five 6s. That is 5 groups of 6: 5 × 6 = 30. 4 × 6 counts the + signs, not the 6s.

items.q: How many dots are there?
items.e: There are 2 rows of 4. Count: 4, 8. So 2 × 4 = 8.
There are 3 rows of 5. Count: 5, 10, 15. So 3 × 5 = 15.
There are 4 rows of 4. Count: 4, 8, 12, 16. So 4 × 4 = 16.
There are 2 rows of 9. Count: 9, 18. So 2 × 9 = 18.
There are 5 rows of 6. Count: 6, 12, 18, 24, 30. So 5 × 6 = 30.

items.q: Which number sentence matches the dots?
items.e: Count the rows: 2. Count one row: 6. 2 rows of 6 is 2 × 6 = 12. 2 + 6 only adds the two numbers.
Count the rows: 3. Count one row: 7. 3 rows of 7 is 3 × 7 = 21. 3 + 7 only adds the two numbers.
Count the rows: 4. Count one row: 5. 4 rows of 5 is 4 × 5 = 20. 4 + 5 only adds the two numbers.
Count the rows: 5. Count one row: 8. 5 rows of 8 is 5 × 8 = 40. 5 + 8 only adds the two numbers.
Rows go across. Count down the side: 3 rows. 6 is the number of dots in each row.
Rows go across. Count down the side: 4 rows. 7 is the number of dots in each row.
Look along one row: 8 dots. 2 is the number of rows.
Turn the dots around. 4 rows of 7 become 7 rows of 4. The number of dots stays the same. So 4 × 7 = 7 × 4 = 28. The answer is 7 × 4.
Turn the dots around. 2 rows of 9 become 9 rows of 2. The number of dots stays the same. So 2 × 9 = 9 × 2 = 18. The answer is 9 × 2.
Turn the dots around. 5 rows of 3 become 3 rows of 5. The number of dots stays the same. So 5 × 3 = 3 × 5 = 15. The answer is 3 × 5.
Turn the dots around. 3 rows of 10 become 10 rows of 3. The number of dots stays the same. So 3 × 10 = 10 × 3 = 30. The answer is 10 × 3.
Turn the dots around. 3 rows of 5 become 5 rows of 3. The number of dots does not change, so 5 × 3 = 15.
Turn the dots around. 2 rows of 7 become 7 rows of 2. The number of dots does not change, so 7 × 2 = 14.
The order can change. The answer stays the same. 4 × 6 = 6 × 4. The missing number is 4. Both make 24.
The order can change. The answer stays the same. 5 × 8 = 8 × 5. The missing number is 5. Both make 40.

items.q: How many socks? Count in 2s.
items.e: Each pair has 2 socks. Count in 2s: 2, 4, 6. There are 6 socks.

items.q: Count in 2s. What comes next?
items.e: Each number is 2 more. 8 + 2 = 10. 9 is counting in 1s.

items.q: How many eyes? Count in 2s.
items.e: Each child has 2 eyes. Count in 2s: 2, 4, 6, 8. There are 8 eyes.

items.q: How many shoes? Count in 2s.
items.e: Each pair has 2 shoes. Count in 2s: 2, 4, 6, 8. There are 8 shoes.

items.q: Count in 2s. What comes next?
items.e: Each number is 2 more. 16 + 2 = 18. 17 is counting in 1s.

items.q: How many socks? Count in 2s.
items.e: Each pair has 2 socks. Count in 2s: 2, 4, 6, 8, 10. There are 10 socks.

items.q: Count in 2s from 0. Which number do you say?
items.e: 0, 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12, 14. When you count in 2s from 0, every number is even. 7, 9 and 15 are odd.

items.q: How many fingers? Count in 5s.
items.e: Each hand has 5 fingers. Count in 5s: 5, 10. There are 10 fingers.

items.q: Count in 5s. What comes next?
items.e: Each number is 5 more. 15 + 5 = 20. 16 is counting in 1s.

items.q: How many fingers? Count in 5s.
items.e: Each hand has 5 fingers. Count in 5s: 5, 10, 15. There are 15 fingers.

items.q: How many petals? Count in 5s.
items.e: Each flower has 5 petals. Count in 5s: 5, 10, 15, 20. There are 20 petals.

items.q: Count in 5s. What comes next?
items.e: Each number is 5 more. 40 + 5 = 45. 41 is counting in 1s.

items.q: Count in 5s from 0. How do the numbers end?
items.e: 0, 5, 10, 15, 20, 25 … The last digit goes 0, 5, 0, 5. So they always end in 0 or 5.

items.q: How many fingers? Count in 5s.
items.e: Each hand has 5 fingers. Count in 5s: 5, 10, 15, 20. There are 20 fingers.

items.q: Each stick has 10 cubes. How many cubes?
items.e: Each stick has 10 cubes. Count in 10s: 10, 20, 30. There are 30 cubes.

items.q: Count in 10s. What comes next?
items.e: Each number is 10 more. 30 + 10 = 40. 31 is counting in 1s.

items.q: How many fingers? Count in 10s.
items.e: Each child shows 2 hands. That is 10 fingers. Count in 10s: 10, 20. There are 20 fingers.

items.q: Each ten frame is full. How many counters?
items.e: A full ten frame has 10 counters. Count in 10s: 10, 20, 30, 40, 50. There are 50 counters.

items.q: Count in 10s. What comes next?
items.e: Each number is 10 more. 60 + 10 = 70. 61 is counting in 1s.

items.q: Each stick has 10 cubes. How many cubes?
items.e: Each stick has 10 cubes. Count in 10s: 10, 20, 30, 40, 50, 60. There are 60 cubes.

items.q: How many apples are there altogether?
items.e: Say one number for each group. Count by 2s: 2, 4, 6. There are 6 apples. (3 is the number of groups, not the apples.)

items.q: How many shells are there altogether?
items.e: Say one number for each group. Count by 2s: 2, 4, 6, 8. There are 8 shells. (4 is the number of groups, not the shells.)
Say one number for each group. Count by 5s: 5, 10. There are 10 stickers. (2 is the number of groups, not the stickers.)

items.q: How many counters are there altogether?
items.e: Say one number for each group. Count by 2s: 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12. There are 12 counters. (6 is the number of groups, not the counters.)
Say one number for each group. Count by 5s: 5, 10, 15. There are 15 strawberries. (3 is the number of groups, not the strawberries.)

items.q: How many counters are there altogether?
items.e: Say one number for each group. Count by 10s: 10, 20. There are 20 counters. (2 is the number of groups, not the counters.)

items.q: How many grapes are there altogether?
items.e: Say one number for each group. Count by 5s: 5, 10, 15, 20. There are 20 grapes. (4 is the number of groups, not the grapes.)

items.q: How many biscuits are there altogether?
items.e: Say one number for each group. Count by 5s: 5, 10, 15, 20, 25. There are 25 biscuits. (5 is the number of groups, not the biscuits.)

items.q: How many counters are there altogether?
items.e: Say one number for each group. Count by 10s: 10, 20, 30, 40. There are 40 counters. (4 is the number of groups, not the counters.)

items.q: Each plate has 3 biscuits. How many biscuits altogether?
items.e: Each plate has 3. There are 2 plates. Add: 3 + 3 = 6. (Not 2: that is just the plates.)

items.q: 4 groups of 2. How many counters altogether?
items.e: There are 4 groups of 2. Count in 2s: 2, 4, 6, 8. That is 8 altogether.
There are 3 groups of 5. Count in 5s: 5, 10, 15. That is 15 altogether.

items.q: How many groups are there?
items.e: Count the circles, not the apples. There are 5 groups, with 2 in each group.
Look inside one circle. It has 5 stars. Every group is the same.

items.q: How many counters? Count in 5s.
items.e: There are 2 rows. Each row has 5. Count in 5s: 5, 10. That is 10.
There are 2 groups of 10. Count in 10s: 10, 20. That is 20 altogether.
There are 4 rows. Each row has 2. Count in 2s: 2, 4, 6, 8. That is 8.

items.q: 6 groups of 2. How many apples altogether?
items.e: There are 6 groups of 2. Count in 2s: 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12. That is 12 altogether.
There are 3 lots of 10. Count in 10s: 10, 20, 30. That is 30 altogether.
There are 3 rows. Each row has 5. Count in 5s: 5, 10, 15. That is 15.
